entries.subject: Placement

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 0.9882 +/- 0.0176 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-669 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). Mass 0.9245 +/- 0.0327 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-669 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). Temperature 5597 +/- 72 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-669 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 5,597 K, because no archive holds a spectrum of this star (stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffeee4. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,597 K and log g 4.41 (u1 0.498, u2 0.235): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.
